$schema-note: Tier 3 of the design brief (2026-08-27) §3.1. One component contract each. A component token exists when a component needs a value the theme may change on its own, and it defaults to a tier 2 token.
$shape-note: A token whose name ends in -rgb names the tier 2 color token it defaults to; the generator emits it in both mode blocks so it follows the mode. Every other token holds a literal CSS value, normally a var() pointing at tier 2.
$scope-note: PR1 shipped the session card, the masthead nameplate, and the two rule contracts. PR2 adds the contracts the six presets and their curated options remap: an option remaps existing tokens and NEVER adds a property name (brief §3.4), so every name a preset file mentions is declared here first. The components that read the PR2 additions land with the schedule and the preset devices in PR3; declaring the contract now is what lets the option data exist as data.

session-card.$stamp-note: The Zine stamp (brief §2.4, 'Exception two'): a flat, unblurred, ink-tinted offset layer at a fixed small distance. Zero offset is the flat-block variant, which every other preset holds.

nameplate.$treatment-note: The three nameplate treatments each preset ships (brief §4) move these four. The rule above the name is the double-rule treatment; the frame is the boxed and framed treatments; the alignment and the metadata placement are the layout. Metadata inside the rule-bounded nameplate block is part of the nameplate device, never an eyebrow (brief §2.4).
nameplate.$corner-mark-note: Atlas draws coordinate marks at two corners of the title block (brief §4.6). A mark states a position, so it appears only where something is being located: every other preset holds zero width and renders no mark at all.

folio-rule.$struck-note: A rule above the folio as well as below it is Zine's struck folio: the typewriter section break of a photocopied programme. Plain text plus rules, never a chip.

$schedule-note: The schedule presentation variants (brief §4, visual stories part 6c). The grid itself lands in PR3; these are the values a preset's variant sets. The agenda number is real sequence data, never zero-padded (brief §2.4).
$plate-note: The Field Guide botanical plate (brief §4.5): a framed drawing with a hairline border and a plate number in the folio style. A plate is drawn linework and never a hero image. The frame is a DOUBLE hairline, drawn as a border plus an outline at the same width. Zero frame and zero pad is the device off: the wrapper then adds no rule, no space, and no reflow, which is what every preset but Field Guide holds.

plate.$number-note: The plate number is real sequence data — day three is PLATE III — never a decorative zero-padded number (brief §2.4). `none` keeps it out of the document and out of the accessibility tree in every preset that is not a plate book.

$specimen-label-note: The Field Guide specimen label (brief §4.5): a small ruled block stating a name, a date, and a place. It carries session metadata and speaker credit lines, it sits below or beside the title it labels, and it is never a chip and never takes a pill radius. Zero rule width, zero padding, and a hidden key is the device off: the block is then the plain caption line it replaced.
$map-grid-note: The Atlas map grid (brief §4.6): a faint coordinate grid behind a section, held below the hairline contrast level, with pointer-events: none. Zero size turns it off.
$route-mark-note: The Atlas route mark (brief §4.6): the line letter in the heading face inside a survey-drawn shape, always with the line's name beside it. A route mark is never a coloured pill, and colour is never the only signal.
$callout-note: Zine's handwritten callout (brief §4.3). --callout-font is a component token, not a fifth semantic role (§3.1, §3.2): one callout per page, real copy, at one fixed angle. A client may point it at var(--font-heading) and drop the script face. Every other preset holds the heading face and a zero angle.
$marginalia-note: The drawn pen marks (Zine) and the pencil line (Field Guide). Its own on/off control, independent of the block variant, and off by default in both presets. A mark never lands on a single word inside a headline, which keeps the system clear of the banned headline-underline trick (brief §2.4).
